<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

With NGRAM speculative decoding, the overlap scheduler (the default) and a grammar-constrained request, `event_loop_overlap` plans the next decode batch, then processes the previous result (the grammar sync), then launches the batch it already planned. If that result finished a request, the request has released its KV and its `req_to_token` row but is launched once more. `_reqs_finishing_inflight` (#42720) only drops a request whose next single token reaches `max_new_tokens`; a verify commits several tokens, and EOS or the end of the grammar is known only after the result is processed.

Example: `unsloth/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`, `--speculative-algorithm NGRAM --speculative-num-draft-tokens 8 --page-size 16`, one request with `regex: "[A-Za-z ,]+"` and `max_new_tokens: 30`. The pending verify reaches 31 output tokens, so the request finishes and frees row 8. The next verify still launches row 8, which is on the free list with `kv_allocated_len == 0`. Its result is discarded and client output is unchanged, but the forward runs on a released row and released pages.

Duplicate-work check: I searched open and closed issues and PRs for NGRAM with grammar or structured output, `grammar_needs_sync`, `is_disable_overlap_for_batch` and finished requests at the grammar sync. #42720 (merged) covers only the one-token length case, #42401 (open) syncs grammar before mixed steps for overlap-capable algorithms, and #25361/#28039 concern the PD decode loop. None covers this case.

## Modifications

- `Scheduler._needs_grammar_sync_before_plan()` is true when a result is pending, the running or last batch holds a grammar request, and the algorithm cannot overlap grammar (NGRAM). In that case `event_loop_overlap` processes the pending result before `get_next_batch_to_run`, so the planner drops the finished requests. Other algorithms and grammar-free batches keep today's order.
- `test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_grammar_sync_before_plan.py` covers decode-to-decode and extend-to-decode iterations in which the pending result finishes the request, and checks that NGRAM without grammar, EAGLE with grammar and non-speculative grammar batches still plan first.
- `event_loop_overlap_disagg_decode` has the same order and is not changed here; PD decode with NGRAM and grammar was not tested.

## Accuracy Tests

```bash
python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_grammar_sync_before_plan.py
python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/managers test/registered/unit/constrained \
  test/registered/unit/speculative test/registered/unit/spec
```

| Tests | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_scheduler_grammar_sync_before_plan.py` (new; 2 finishing-result cases, 3 order controls) | the 2 finishing-result cases fail: the finished request is launched | all 5 pass |
| `managers`, `constrained`, `speculative` and `spec` suites | 1,542 passed | 1,544 passed |

The suites show the same failures on both trees: two multimodal feature-pool tests, one DFlash config test, and one module that needs the missing `parameterized` package.

End to end, one server, 58 sequential `/generate` requests (regex and JSON-schema pairs, length-bounded regex, a terminating regex, unconstrained controls), with an observation-only wrapper on `Scheduler.run_batch`:

| Tree | Runs | Launches of already-finished requests | Client outputs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main | 2 | 33 and 33 (every grammar request ending in EOS; 15 of 18 ending by length) | 58/58 HTTP 200 |
| main, `--disable-overlap-schedule` | 1 | 0 | identical |
| this PR | 2 | 0 and 0 | identical |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Only NGRAM batches holding a grammar request lose planning overlap, and those already wait for the previous result before launch. Unconstrained batches take the unchanged path.

Setup: 8 concurrent requests, NGRAM 8, on an RTX A6000 with no other jobs. Main and this PR were launched alternately, with two repeats per launch. Each cell is the mean output throughput, with the range in parentheses.

| Workload | main (tok/s) | this PR (tok/s) | Diff |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 32 requests x 128 tokens, grammar | 3,048 (2,738 to 3,161) | 3,125 (2,860 to 3,243) | +2.5% |
| 32 requests x 128 tokens, unconstrained | 5,697 (5,435 to 5,777) | 5,490 (4,983 to 5,779) | -3.6% |
| 64 requests x 256 tokens, grammar | 3,095 (3,017 to 3,191) | 3,104 (3,015 to 3,228) | +0.3% |
| 64 requests x 256 tokens, unconstrained | 5,876 (5,751 to 5,985) | 5,918 (5,841 to 6,044) | +0.7% |

The short workload had six launches of main and five of this PR, and each phase lasts under a second. The longer workload had three launches of each and shows no difference.

## AI assistance

Claude Code assisted with the investigation, implementation, tests and drafting.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

files.patch:
@@ -2095,15 +2095,22 @@ def pop_and_process():
                 self._record_scheduler_state_for_paused_engine()
                 continue
 
+            # A host-draft grammar batch waits for the last result anyway; process
+            # it before planning so the plan drops the requests it finishes.
+            processed_before_plan = self._needs_grammar_sync_before_plan()
+            if processed_before_plan:
+                pop_and_process()
+
             # Get the next batch to run
             plan = self.get_next_batch_to_run(
                 running_batch=self.running_batch, last_batch=self.last_batch
             )
             self.running_batch = plan.running_batch
             batch = plan.batch_to_run
             self.cur_batch_for_debug = batch
-            disable_overlap_for_batch = self.is_disable_overlap_for_batch(
-                batch, last_batch=self.last_batch
+            disable_overlap_for_batch = (
+                not processed_before_plan
+                and self.is_disable_overlap_for_batch(batch, last_batch=self.last_batch)
             )
 
             # If we do not need to overlap the current batch with the last batch,
@@ -2131,7 +2138,7 @@ def pop_and_process():
 
             # Process the last batch
             if self.last_batch:
-                if not disable_overlap_for_batch:
+                if not (disable_overlap_for_batch or processed_before_plan):
                     pop_and_process()
             elif batch is None:
                 # When the server is idle, do self-check and re-init some states
@@ -2148,6 +2155,28 @@ def pop_and_process():
             if envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_STRICT_MEM_CHECK_DURING_BUSY.get():
                 self.invariant_checker.self_check_during_busy()
 
+    def _needs_grammar_sync_before_plan(self) -> bool:
+        """Whether to process the pending result before planning the next batch.
+
+        A host-draft algorithm (NGRAM) processes the previous result before it
+        launches a grammar decode batch (see is_disable_overlap_for_batch). With
+        the plan made first, a request that result finishes (a multi-token run
+        reaching max_new_tokens, an EOS, the grammar end) would be launched after
+        its KV and request row were released. Conservative: true whenever the
+        next batch may hold a grammar request.
+        """
+        if not self.result_queue:
+            return False
+        last_batch = self.last_batch
+        if not self.running_batch.has_grammar and not (
+            last_batch is not None and last_batch.has_grammar
+        ):
+            return False
+        return (
+            not self.spec_algorithm.is_none()
+            and not self.spec_algorithm.supports_grammar_overlap()
+        )
+
     def is_disable_overlap_for_batch(
         self, batch: ScheduleBatch, last_batch: Optional[ScheduleBatch]
     ) -> bool:

@@ -0,0 +1,121 @@
+"""The overlap loop must not launch a host-draft grammar batch with a request
+that the previous result, processed at the grammar sync, already finished."""
+
+import unittest
+from array import array
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock
+
+from sglang.srt.managers.schedule_batch import FINISH_LENGTH, Req, ScheduleBatch
+from sglang.srt.managers.scheduler import Scheduler
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.forward_batch_info import ForwardMode
+from sglang.srt.sampling.sampling_params import SamplingParams
+from sglang.srt.speculative.spec_info import SpeculativeAlgorithm
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+def _make_req() -> Req:
+    sampling_params = SamplingParams(max_new_tokens=8)
+    sampling_params.normalize(None)
+    req = Req(
+        rid="r",
+        origin_input_text="",
+        origin_input_ids=array("q", [1, 2, 3]),
+        sampling_params=sampling_params,
+        vocab_size=128,
+    )
+    # Four tokens in: the next single token cannot finish it by length, so
+    # only processing the pending result reveals that it finished.
+    req.output_ids.extend([4, 5, 6, 7])
+    return req
+
+
+def _run_two_iterations(spec_algorithm, has_grammar, first_mode=ForwardMode.DECODE):
+    """Drive event_loop_overlap through two plans of one request whose first
+    result finishes it (a multi-token run reaching max_new_tokens)."""
+    req = _make_req()
+    events, launched = [], []
+
+    def make_batch(reqs, mode):
+        return ScheduleBatch(
+            reqs=reqs,
+            forward_mode=mode,
+            spec_algorithm=spec_algorithm,
+            has_grammar=has_grammar,
+        )
+
+    scheduler = Scheduler.__new__(Scheduler)
+    scheduler.gracefully_exit = False
+    scheduler.ingest_requests = MagicMock(side_effect=[[], [], StopIteration])
+    scheduler._engine_paused = False
+    scheduler.require_mlp_sync = False
+    scheduler.enable_unified_memory = False
+    scheduler.is_generation = False
+    scheduler.spec_algorithm = spec_algorithm
+    # A prefill runs from an empty running batch and merges at the next plan.
+    first_is_decode = first_mode.is_decode()
+    scheduler.running_batch = ScheduleBatch(reqs=[req] if first_is_decode else [])
+    scheduler.running_batch.has_grammar = has_grammar and first_is_decode
+    scheduler.last_batch = None
+    scheduler._apply_war_barrier = MagicMock()
+
+    def get_next_batch_to_run(*, running_batch, last_batch):
+        events.append("plan")
+        if last_batch is None:
+            return MagicMock(
+                running_batch=running_batch, batch_to_run=make_batch([req], first_mode)
+            )
+        # Like the real planner: finished requests leave the running batch.
+        live = [r for r in [req] if not r.finished()]
+        batch = make_batch(live, ForwardMode.DECODE) if live else None
+        return MagicMock(running_batch=running_batch, batch_to_run=batch)
+
+    def run_batch(batch):
+        events.append("run")
+        launched.append([(r.rid, r.finished()) for r in batch.reqs])
+        return object()
+
+    def process_batch_result(batch, result):
+        events.append("process")
+        # The committed run finishes the request, which releases its KV row.
+        req.output_ids.extend([8, 9, 10, 11])
+        req.finished_reason = FINISH_LENGTH(length=8)
+
+    scheduler.get_next_batch_to_run = get_next_batch_to_run
+    scheduler.run_batch = run_batch
+    scheduler.process_batch_result = process_batch_result
+
+    with unittest.TestCase().assertRaises(StopIteration):
+        scheduler.event_loop_overlap()
+    return events, launched
+
+
+class TestGrammarSyncBeforePlan(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_ngram_grammar_result_is_processed_before_next_plan(self):
+        for first_mode in (ForwardMode.DECODE, ForwardMode.EXTEND):
+            with self.subTest(first_mode=first_mode.name):
+                events, launched = _run_two_iterations(
+                    SpeculativeAlgorithm.NGRAM, True, first_mode
+                )
+                # The finished request is never launched again.
+                self.assertEqual(launched, [[("r", False)]])
+                self.assertEqual(events, ["plan", "run", "process", "plan"])
+
+    def test_overlapping_algorithms_keep_plan_before_process(self):
+        cases = (
+            (SpeculativeAlgorithm.NGRAM, False),
+            (SpeculativeAlgorithm.EAGLE, True),
+            (SpeculativeAlgorithm.NONE, True),
+        )
+        for spec_algorithm, has_grammar in cases:
+            with self.subTest(spec=spec_algorithm.name, grammar=has_grammar):
+                events, launched = _run_two_iterations(spec_algorithm, has_grammar)
+                # Ordinary overlap: the second batch launches before the first
+                # result is processed, so the request is still live at launch.
+                self.assertEqual(launched, [[("r", False)], [("r", False)]])
+                self.assertEqual(events, ["plan", "run", "plan", "run", "process"])
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
